item.title: Pace Prints Heads West With a Hollywood Hub, a Chuck Close Deep Dive, and a Case for Why Prints Matter Now
item.description: Prints have “become part of the conversation again” because artists are treating them as serious works, made by hand, and presented “at a value point… where more people can participate.”

item.title: Controversial Right-Wing French Culture Minister Stepping Down to Run for Mayor of Paris
item.description: She ran and lost the last mayoral election in 2020.

item.title: Judy Baca Denies Allegations She Improperly Profited From $5 M. Grant for ‘Great Wall’ Expansion
item.description: According to tax filings cited by the Times, Baca’s salary rose from roughly $50,000 in the years before the Mellon award to more than $200,000 annually after the grant was secured.

item.title: Chicago’s DePaul Art Museum to Close After 40 Years
item.description: The school faces serious financial challenges.

item.title: Sagrada Familia’s Central Tower Is Finished, 144 Years After Construction Began
item.description: Work on the landmark in Barcelona is expected to continue for another decade.

item.title: Rena Bransten, Legendary San Francisco Art Dealer, Dies at 92
item.description: John Waters called her a "classy act and a great art dealer ahead of her time.”

item.title: SoCal’s Bunny Museum Receives Gift of Rabbit Sculpture
item.description: The museum, which was destroyed in 2025’s Eaton Fire, plans to reopen in a new building in 2028

item.title: Ulysses Jenkins, Video Art Trailblazer with an Eye on Mass Media, Has Died at 79
